answer: Each identity tends one orchard anchor tree and locks a 70-credit bond to its key. At bloom it files plume counts with branch photos. An auditor resamples three marked branches and scales their plume count to the anchor crown by the filed orchard branch map. A count outside 5% or a reused photo burns the bond. The first tree costs 37 credits, the kth costs 37+5(k-1), the 1000th 5032, and 1000 fakes cost 2,534,500 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-count ring fails because resampled branches carry the tree key tag. An honest tender pays 37 once and recovers the bond.
